company_items.summary: AutoZone reported FQ4 EPS of $56.05 vs. the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — driven by a 145 basis point tailwind to gross margins from tariff refunds and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit. Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% vs. the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional ~$106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80-90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex deeper into the robotics and Physical AI ecosystem.

MillerKnoll posted solid FQ1 EPS of 53 cents vs. the Street's 36 cents, and importantly the beat holds up even excluding an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind — clean EPS of 42 cents still topped consensus. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. the Street's $943.2 million, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed to $3.88-4.03 billion from $3.93-4.13 billion, while the EPS range of $1.85-2.15 was left unchanged.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1st, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. The appointment is a straightforward leadership transition with no financial guidance update attached.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS at 78 cents vs. the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% — well below the Street's 13.85% estimate — pressured by higher material costs. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressure on household budgets as headwinds keeping retail soft. Some bright spots emerged: dealer inventory is at healthy levels, structural cost actions are underway, and the North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year, though the company won't issue formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. The result is a meaningful data point in the competitive GLP-1 obesity drug landscape. The strong efficacy readout drove an immediate positive market reaction.

sectors: RV/recreational vehicle sector under pressure given THOR's weak gross margins and cautious macro commentary around consumer budgets and retail softness. GLP-1/obesity drug space gets a positive catalyst from Viking's VK2735 trial results showing 22% weight loss.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday September 22nd — there's no broad macro or Fed commentary in today's newsletter, so let's go straight through the names reporting before the open.

Starting with AutoZone. The company beat on earnings per share — fifty-six dollars and five cents versus the Street's fifty-four dollars and three cents — but the quality is questionable. The upside was driven almost entirely by tariff refunds, which added 145 basis points to gross margins, and a non-cash LIFO accounting benefit worth another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the picture gets murky fast. Domestic comps came in at plus 1.6% versus expectations of plus 3.1% — a meaningful miss — and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management said sales improved in the final eight weeks of the quarter and they feel well-positioned heading into fiscal 2027, but this is a low-quality beat and the tape may reflect that.

Next, Cognex is acquiring RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision tech for robotic perception and Physical AI — for roughly 500 million dollars upfront plus an additional 106 and a half million. RealSense is expected to generate 80 to 90 million dollars in revenue with more than 50% year-over-year growth. This is a strategic move deeper into the robotics and Physical AI buildout and should be viewed positively.

MillerKnoll posted a strong earnings beat — 53 cents versus 36 cents expected — and crucially, the beat holds up even excluding the tariff refund tailwind. Clean earnings were 42 cents, still well above consensus. Sales missed at 923 million versus 943 million expected, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year sales guidance was trimmed modestly while the earnings per share range was left unchanged. A mixed but mostly solid print.

THOR Industries disappointed. Earnings per share came in at 78 cents versus 87 cents expected, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% — nearly 150 basis points below the Street's estimate. Management blamed stubborn interest rates, high fuel costs, and inflation squeezing consumer budgets. They expect a relatively flat retail environment in fiscal 2027 and won't give formal guidance until later this fall. On the bright side, the North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year, and structural cost actions are being taken. But this is a bearish print overall.

Finally, Viking Therapeutics is the standout mover this morning. Shares are spiking pre-market after the company reported 22% weight loss in its clinical trial for VK2735, its GLP-1 obesity drug. That's a strong efficacy result in one of the most watched therapeutic areas in the market right now. Clearly bullish for Viking.

Bottom line for today: no broad directional market call in this note. It's a stock-picker's morning. Watch Viking on GLP-1 momentum, Cognex on the acquisition response, and THOR for any read-through on consumer discretionary and the RV space.
